title: Classes and Objects
summary: Defining your own classes with fields, constructors and instance methods, creating objects with new, the this reference, references and null, toString, object identity versus equality, and how to design a class around the data it owns.

cards.q: What is the difference between a class and an object?
cards.a:
A class is the blueprint; an object is one instance made from it with `new`, with its own field values

The class describes the fields and methods. Each `new` creates a separate instance, and every instance has its own copy of the fields.

cards.q: What does `this.name = name;` do in a constructor?
cards.a:
Copies the parameter `name` into the object's field called `name`

`this` is the object being constructed, so `this.name` is its field, while plain `name` is the parameter that hides it.

cards.q: `Point a = new Point(1, 2); Point b = new Point(1, 2);` Without an `equals` override, what is `a.equals(b)`?
cards.a:
false

`Object.equals` compares references unless the class overrides it, and `a` and `b` are two different objects.
